notes:
Key account: Glacier Runway AI — freight-routing & dynamic scheduling platform. CTO (M. Alvarez) wants deterministic inference economics for customer SLAs. Current ask: firm throughput guarantees and clear burst rules before committing to 12-month reserved capacity.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-01-15: Intro call (Sofia R.). High-level requirements: sub-200ms p95 for short prompts (<=512 tokens), sustain high token throughput for nightly re-ranks.
- 2026-01-28: Architecture deep-dive (Daniel C.). They run multi-tenant job queues; want per-tenant isolation policies and token quotas.
- 2026-02-09: Fireflies call ff_4372_20260212 — discussed model variants and fallback to 8-bit quantized weights. CTO quote: "We need predictable per-hour token capacity; spikes from routing bursts mustn't blow our cost model."
- 2026-02-20: Onsite POC kickoff — we provisioned a 4-GPU H100 pool (short burst testing). POC metrics attached in drive doc.
- 2026-03-05: Redwood perf team delivered first throughput run (attached). Observed: sustained 48k tokens/sec for standard 2k-context rerank workload across pool of 4 H100s; bursts up to ~110k tokens/sec for 2 minutes before queuing grew.
- 2026-03-08: Procurement + Engineering sync (Sofia, Daniel, Aisha). Legal flagged residency clause and SLA addendum for throughput guarantees.

Requirements summary (customer stated):
- Primary workload: nightly reranking + customer-facing chat (real-time) with mixed request sizes.
- Target sustained throughput: minimum 60,000 tokens/sec for nightly pipelines (8-hour window).
- Concurrency cap expectation: support 500 concurrent chat sessions with 95th p50 response times within 200-350ms for short prompts.
- Burst policy: allow short bursts up to 200% of sustained capacity for <=5 minutes per hour; excess should be queued or routed to cheaper fallback model, not dropped.
- Latency SLOs: p95 <=200ms (<=512 tokens), p99 <=650ms (>=2048 tokens).
- Model preferences: open-models with Redwood-verified runtimes; prefer FP16/H100 kernel path, willing to accept q4_0/q8_0 for fallback.
- Reserved GPU planning: initial ask 8x H100 or equivalent (aim for headroom); want clear mapping from reserved GPU count -> guaranteed tokens/sec and concurrency.
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, customer-managed KMS, 7-year audit log retention (for audits).

Negotiation points being worked:
- Minimum tokens/sec guarantee to include in SLA (customer pushing for 60k sustained; our capacity plan currently guarantees 50k for 8x H100, 48k observed on 4x pool).
- Formal concurrency caps per account (500 sessions) vs. soft concurrency with fair-share queuing.
- Burst policy specifics: length, cooling period, billing for burst overages, and automatic fallback to quantized variants.
- Penalty/credits for missed throughput SLOs and measurement windows (they want hourly accounting, we propose rolling 8-hour window).
- Hardware commitment: customer prefers H100; Redwood offered mixed pool option (H100 + cheaper GPU for non-latency-critical reranks).

Action items / next steps:
- Redwood infra to provide revised capacity-to-throughput table mapping (tokens/sec per reserved GPU config) by 2026-03-15. (Daniel)
- Legal to draft SLA addendum with hourly measurement method and credit formula; aim to share 2026-03-18. (Sofia + Legal)
- Arrange second POC run on 8x H100 equivalent pool focusing on sustained 8-hour window (schedule for week of 2026-03-22). (Daniel + Infra)
public_notes: Procurement-heavy; throughput guarantees are the gating item. Customer expects explicit tokens/sec guarantees + burst policy. Pricing will be tied to reserved GPU count + burst billing.
